summary: Configured inventory-worker as an enabled systemd service running /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker under the dedicated inventorysvc system account. The service and account persisted across node1’s required reboot. Ubuntu 24.04.3 and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Created the inventorysvc system user and group with no interactive login.
Created, validated, enabled, and started inventory-worker.service.
Verified the exact executable runs under UID 999/GID 988.
Rebooted node1 safely and confirmed its boot identity changed.
Verified the node, account, service, and worker process recovered after reboot.

evidence.summary: The unit validated and enabled successfully; before and after reboot it was loaded, enabled, active/running, and its ExecStart was the requested worker path.

evidence.requirement: Run under the dedicated inventorysvc account
evidence.summary: The dedicated no-login system account was created, and direct process inspection showed the worker running as inventorysvc with UID 999 and GID 988.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Initial, post-configuration, and post-reboot checks consistently showed Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic.

Healthy baseline used boot ID cf34dc87-fdca-4c6a-80e1-579d5524a1da; reboot scheduling was acknowledged; node1 returned with changed boot ID 82d0568e-c3d4-47c9-9228-0fa1fe41927d; systemd reported the system running and inventory-worker enabled, active, and running under inventorysvc.
